query: Nansen smart money label Hyperliquid leaderboard losing trader copy trade reverse fade
content:
**Nansen labels "Smart Money" (or similar high-performing trader categories) on Hyperliquid based on historical profitability, trade patterns, wallet behavior, and other on-chain metrics across chains.** [[1]](https://coinmarketman.com/blog/hyperliquid-data-providers-compared/) [[2]](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14800361-nansen-smart-money-how-it-works)

These labels help identify skilled traders, funds, or whales versus retail. Nansen integrates deeply with Hyperliquid perps data, offering leaderboards, smart money trade tracking, and filters. [[3]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid/hyperliquid-leaderboard)

### Nansen Hyperliquid Leaderboard Features
Nansen's API and dashboard provide perpetual trading leaderboards ranked by **PnL** (profit and loss), ROI, account value, etc., over custom date ranges (e.g., 24h, 7d, 30d). [[4]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/profiler/hyperliquid-address-leaderboard)

- **Key filters** include trader address labels like "Smart Money," account value minimums, and PnL thresholds.
- You can isolate **Smart Money** leaders to see top performers with their PnL, ROI, and labels. [[3]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid/hyperliquid-leaderboard)
- Endpoints like `/perp-leaderboard` return addresses + labels. There are also dedicated Smart Money Perp Trades for real-time activity from labeled wallets. [[5]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid/smart-money-perp-trades)
- Dashboard views (e.g., app.nansen.ai) show Hyperliquid Perps Leaderboard with Smart Money focus. [[6]](https://app.nansen.ai/smart-money?chains=hyperliquid)

**Note:** Leaderboards primarily rank *profitable* traders (positive PnL). For "losing traders," sort by lowest/negative PnL, use custom filters, or analyze broader wallet PnL distributions. Nansen doesn't prominently feature a "top losers" public list, as its value is in highlighting winners/smart wallets. [[3]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid/hyperliquid-leaderboard)

Hyperliquid's native leaderboard (app.hyperliquid.xyz/leaderboard) shows top PNL winners by timeframes (e.g., 30D), with filters excluding small accounts. It does not natively emphasize losers. [[7]](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/leaderboard)

### Copy Trading vs. Reverse/Fade Strategies on Hyperliquid
**Copy trading** (mirroring top/Smart Money traders) is popular due to on-chain transparency. Tools/platforms support auto-copying Hyperliquid wallets, including from Nansen-labeled smart ones. [[8]](https://www.bitmex.com/app/leaderboard/copy-leader/hyperliquid) [[9]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid)

- **Pros of copying Smart Money**: Access to proven performers via Nansen labels + leaderboards. Some simulations show positive returns when following larger-account whales (e.g., ≥$5M–$10M thresholds). [[10]](https://medium.com/@gwrx2005/combining-simulation-and-machine-learning-analysis-of-whale-trading-on-hyperliquid-93f10d96941b)
- **Risks**: Past performance ≠ future; many "whales" or leaderboard traders have drawdowns. Most Hyperliquid traders overall lose money (e.g., analyses show only ~14% profitable in some periods). [[11]](https://beincrypto.com/hyperliquid-traders-profitability/)

**Reverse copy / fade** (taking the opposite side of a trader's positions) is explicitly supported on some copy-trading platforms for Hyperliquid. [[8]](https://www.bitmex.com/app/leaderboard/copy-leader/hyperliquid) [[12]](https://www.bitmex.com/blog/how-to-copy-trade-hyperliquid)

- **Rationale for fading losers**: If a wallet consistently shows negative PnL or poor timing (identifiable via Nansen profiling or Hyperliquid data), reversing their longs/shorts can theoretically profit from their mistakes. Some tools flag "terrible" traders for reverse strategies. [[13]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3V04vFddFRA)
- **Caveats**: This is high-risk. Markets can stay irrational longer than expected; a "loser" might reverse or have asymmetric upside. Large losers can still influence liquidity or trigger cascades. Always use tight risk management (stops, position sizing). Simulations highlight concentration risk and the need for ongoing validation. [[10]](https://medium.com/@gwrx2005/combining-simulation-and-machine-learning-analysis-of-whale-trading-on-hyperliquid-93f10d96941b)

### Practical Tips
- **Use Nansen** for Smart Money filtering on Hyperliquid leaderboards and real-time perp trades. Combine with wallet profiling for context (e.g., sub-labels, historical consistency). [[9]](https://docs.nansen.ai/api/hyperliquid)
- Check Hyperliquid native leaderboard for raw top performers, then cross-reference addresses in Nansen for labels. [[7]](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/leaderboard)
- For copy/reverse: Platforms like BitMEX (integrated support) or others allow one-click copy/reverse with AUM, PnL tracking. [[12]](https://www.bitmex.com/blog/how-to-copy-trade-hyperliquid)
- Broader context: Perps trading is zero-sum (minus fees); a small % of traders capture most profits. Focus on risk management over blind following.

For the latest specific wallets or performance, check Nansen's dashboard/API directly (requires access) or current Hyperliquid leaderboard, as data changes rapidly. Always DYOR and trade responsibly—crypto perps involve high leverage risk.

sources.description:
Reverse copy trading—also known as inverse or fade trading—turns a losing trading system on its head. Instead of following a lead trader or bot’s every move, reverse copying does the opposite: when the master account buys, you sell, and vice versa.   
  
 This counterintuitive approach is rooted in the mathematics of expectancy. If a strategy consistently loses, betting against it (factoring in costs) can produce positive returns. But, like all edge-seeking methods, it requires nuance, discipline, and the right technology—like Copygram’s advanced copier with Reverse Mode.

 Reverse Copy Trading: Mirror a losing trader by executing the opposite trades
 Fade Losing Traders: Capitalize on consistently poor performers
 Hedge Exposure: Offset risk by betting against correlated strategies [...] It may seem counterintuitive to follow a trader just to do the opposite of their trades. However, in many markets—especially retail Forex and crypto—most traders lose over time due to poor risk management or flawed strategies.   
  
Reverse copying lets you profit from this predictable failure. If a trading bot or human consistently delivers negative returns, inverting can create a positive edge (after costs). This technique is also popular among contrarian traders who fade market sentiment.

 Hedging: Use reverse trades to protect a basket of correlated positions
 Fading "herd" bots: Run reverse mode on bots that crowd into losing trades
 Testing Prop Firm bots: Identify failing strategies in competitions and fade them [...] ## Q&A: Top Questions About Reverse Copying Answered

 Is it legal/ethical to reverse copy traders?   
  ✅ Yes, as long as your broker/platform allows it and you’re not violating any terms. Reverse copying is simply a sophisticated use of market order flows.
 Is reverse copy trading suitable for beginners?   
  ⚠️ Not unless they fully understand the math of expectancy, drawdown, and trading costs. It’s best for advanced users.
 How do I identify a truly failing bot or trader?   
  Look for long-term negative returns, high consistency in losses, and low success across multiple market cycles.
 Is Copygram’s reverse mode customizable?   
  Yes. You can selectively enable reverse mode per master, symbol, and adjust lot sizes as needed.

### 🚀 Final Thoughts: Smart Contrarians Win
